items.stem: Which transport protocol should a developer choose when every byte must arrive, in order, without loss?

options.text: TCP, because it provides ordered, reliable, connection-oriented delivery
options.rationale: Correct: TCP handles retransmission, ordering and flow control for reliable streams.
UDP is connectionless and gives no ordering or delivery guarantee.
ARP is a link-layer address-resolution protocol, not a transport.
ICMP is for control/diagnostics, not reliable data transport.

items.explanation: Correct: TCP handles retransmission, ordering and flow control for reliable streams.

items.stem: Which statements about HTTP are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: HTTP is stateless; state is carried via cookies or tokens
options.rationale: Correct: each request is independent, so applications add state with cookies/tokens.

options.text: A 404 status means the requested resource was not found
options.rationale: Correct: 404 is the standard not-found client-error status.

options.text: A 200 status indicates a server error
options.rationale: 200 means success; 5xx codes indicate server errors.

options.text: HTTP requires a new TCP connection for every object in HTTP/2
options.rationale: HTTP/2 multiplexes many streams over one connection, reducing connections.

items.explanation: Correct: each request is independent, so applications add state with cookies/tokens.; Correct: 404 is the standard not-found client-error status.

items.stem: What does NAT (Network Address Translation) primarily do?

options.text: Maps private internal addresses to one or more public addresses so hosts can share them
options.rationale: Correct: NAT lets many private hosts reach the internet through shared public addresses.

options.text: Encrypts all traffic leaving the network
options.rationale: NAT does not encrypt; that is the role of TLS/VPNs.
MAC addresses are hardware-assigned, not set by NAT.

options.text: Resolves domain names to IP addresses
options.rationale: Name resolution is DNS, not NAT.

items.explanation: Correct: NAT lets many private hosts reach the internet through shared public addresses.
